content: In a study involving 74 participants, 42 adverse events related to the study drug were reported in 30 individuals (41%). These events included the need for additional intravenous fluids during pentamidine administration (10 cases), a reduction in the infusion rate of pentamidine, oral hydration (2 cases), extended hospital observation (2 cases), additional medication during pentamidine infusion (2 cases), and glucose supplementation (1 case). Regarding follow-up, one study (Ethiopia, 2015) reported that 5% of participants were lost to follow-up after one year, and 14% (10 out of 74) were lost after two years. In another study (Ethiopia, 2019b), all patients who began secondary prophylaxis were followed until the study's conclusion. No studies were identified that reported on patient satisfaction with secondary prophylaxis. The certainty of evidence for outcomes such as relapse-free survival and treatment adherence was rated as very low due to limitations in study design and data quality. In terms of mortality, one study (Ethiopia, 2015) reported that 17% (5 out of 29) of participants with baseline CD4 counts below 200/µL died within one year. Another study (Ethiopia, 2019b) reported a 7% mortality rate (5 out of 74) after two years. Relapse rates were also significant, with 41% (12 out of 29) of participants with low CD4 counts experiencing relapse, and two of these patients later died. The estimated probability of relapse-free survival at 12 months was 71% (95% CI: 59–80%) in one study (Ethiopia, 2015). Another study (Ethiopia, 2019b) reported that 46% (95% CI: 26–63%) of participants with low CD4 counts achieved relapse-free survival at 12 months. Treatment adherence varied between studies. In one study, 55% (41 out of 74) of participants completed follow-up, taking at least 11 out of 12 doses without experiencing relapse, death, or serious adverse events. In another study, 76% (22 out of 29) of participants achieved 100% compliance with monthly pentamidine infusions. Serious adverse events were reported in 23% (17 out of 74) of participants in one study, with two cases of renal failure potentially linked to pentamidine. Another study reported serious adverse events in 28% (8 out of 29) of participants, including one death due to acute renal failure in a patient with multiple coexisting conditions. No studies reported on patient or healthcare worker preferences or values related to intravenous liposomal amphotericin B and oral miltefosine combination therapy. Additionally, no studies stratified intervention effects by gender or age. Most participants were adults aged 21–64 years, with a mean age of 37 in monotherapy and 33 in combination therapy groups. The teratogenic potential of miltefosine necessitates the use of reliable contraception during treatment and for four months afterward. Oral contraceptives were deemed inadequate due to the high prevalence of vomiting and diarrhea associated with miltefosine treatment.
